title: Frohmanian symplectic tether, May 31 fixed-kappa T3 form

claims.statement: Degeneracy: the tether with kappa = C_CZ(3) satisfies B(F, H) = 0 for the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian H (C2).
kappa := C_CZ(3), the universal 3D Calderon-Zygmund constant, with C_CZ(3) > 0.
Step 4: the feedback coefficient is fixed by C3; kappa = C_CZ(3) is the minimal strength absorbing the stretching term +C_CZ M^2 (Young, eps = kappa/4).

Theorem 2.3: any antisymmetric B that is invariant under the coadjoint action of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of T3 (C1), degenerate w.r.t. kinetic energy (C2), and produces controllable negative feedback with coefficient exactly -kappa M^2 (C3) equals the TetherKernel with kappa = C_CZ(3).
The TetherKernel with kappa = C_CZ(3) satisfies C1, C2, C3.
Tether bounding inequality: d/dt ||omega||_inf <= C - kappa ||omega||_inf^2 with kappa > 0, hence ||omega||_inf stays bounded.
TetherKernel is the Biot-Savart double integral weighted by pointwise |omega(x)|^2.
Navier-Stokes vorticity on T3 obeys the tether bounding inequality (estimates layer).

306cd9f98c70.question: Q4 (author-review question, recorded through the harness store; not generated by the heuristic matcher): Theorem 2.3 says "antisymmetric" (L222), which makes it only vacuously true, while the tether kernel is symmetric. Did you mean the tether in Theorem 2.3 to be symmetric or antisymmetric?
